analysis.hypothesis: Reference model applies torch.abs followed by torch.floor. Each operation is elementwise with identical shape/dtype/device. I will define a single custom op custom_abs_floor that performs both steps sequentially, matching the reference semantics exactly without using torch operators. The normal forward calls this custom op, while debug_forward yields intermediate checkpoints by calling two separate custom ops: custom_abs for step_001 and custom_floor for step_002, then returns the final tensor. However, to avoid redundant computation and maintain exact reference order, I will define distinct custom ops for each reference computation step: custom_abs and custom_floor. In normal forward I will call both sequentially, guaranteeing semantic equivalence and allowing debug_forward to yield intermediate results from the same computations without recomputation. This keeps the implementation straightforward and matches the reference exactly. The custom ops will operate on contiguous CUDA float32 tensors only, as exercised by the reference; no other dtypes/devices need support.

analysis.hypothesis: custom_abs and custom_floor are simple elementwise operations on contiguous float32 CUDA tensors. We can implement them as two separate CUDA kernels with grid-stride loops, each with a launcher that takes raw pointers and a CUDA stream. The Python binding will be provided in the next stage; here we only need to export C-style launcher functions.

Only floating-point abs and floor required; no other dtypes requested.
